S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.

subtypes.Depressed Mood: A persistently sunken mood or feeling of depression.
subtypes.Tearfulness: A state of frequent crying or inability to hold back tears.
subtypes.Sadness: A state where a sad or gloomy mood is maintained continuously.
subtypes.Emptiness: A feeling of inner emptiness or a state of feeling no emotion.
subtypes.Emotional Numbness: A state where emotions feel dulled or paralyzed.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.

subtypes.Significant Weight Loss: Weight loss of more than 5% in a month without dieting.
subtypes.Weight Gain: Weight gain of more than 5% in a month.
subtypes.Decrease in Appetite: Decrease in appetite occurring nearly every day.
subtypes.Increase in Appetite: Increase in appetite occurring nearly every day.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.

subtypes.Chronic Fatigue: Fatigue that persists for a long period even after adequate rest.
subtypes.Physical Fatigue: A state of physical exhaustion where the body feels heavy and easily tires even from minor activities.
subtypes.Mental Fatigue: A state where fatigue accumulates rapidly during the process of thinking or concentrating.
subtypes.Loss of Energy: Difficulty performing daily activities due to a decline in energy and vitality.

symptom.disease_info: Persistent Depressive Disorder (dysthymia) is a chronic mood disorder characterized by a consistently low or dysthymic mood lasting at least two years in adults, with no extended periods of full remission. Individuals often function day-to-day but at a reduced level, experiencing a long-standing sense of gloom, low motivation, and other depressive features that become part of their perceived personality. Clinically, it differs from major depressive disorder by its chronicity and typically milder, more insidious presentation, though episodes of major depression can occur on top of it ("double depression"). It is frequently under-recognized because patients and families may attribute the symptoms to character or life circumstances rather than a treatable illness, and impairment is often seen in social, occupational, or academic domains over time.

patient.stressor: For Nikeita, the difficulties started after she transitioned from full-time college coursework into a demanding QA inspector job on rotating shifts while continuing part-time classes about two and a half years ago. Initially energized by the responsibility and the steady paycheck, she gradually found that the irregular hours, constant attention to production quotas, and pressure to prove herself as one of the youngest on the line left little time or energy for basketball league games, dancing nights, or STEM volunteering that used to ground her. Over the next 2 years and 4 months, this imbalance slowly became her new normal: she kept up appearances with friends but often skipped practices or social events at the last minute, blaming work or school, and told herself she just needed to "push through" until she could move up to a better role. She finally sought help after a supervisor commented on her reduced engagement and a close friend from church pointed out that she hadn’t seemed like her usual upbeat, competitive self for a long time, which made her realize how long she had been feeling this way and prompted her to ask her campus health clinic for a mental health referral.
patient.chief_complaint: My sleep has been messed up for a long time, and no matter how I change my schedule I can’t seem to get any real rest.

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.
S024.manifestation: For a long time now, even on days when nothing actually goes wrong, I just feel this low, gray heaviness in the background, like I’m going through the motions at work and school without ever really feeling excited or genuinely happy about anything anymore.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.
S026.manifestation: I used to be all about grabbing food with my teammates or trying new places after class, but now most days I’m just not hungry, I kind of pick at whatever’s around or skip meals on shift and only realize later that I barely ate all day.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.
S027.manifestation: With the rotating shifts my sleep is all over the place, but what really gets me is that even on nights when I’m actually home and in bed on time, I lie there for an hour or more with my mind circling around work quotas and homework, then wake up a couple times in the middle of the night and never feel like I got real rest.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.
S029.manifestation: I feel tired pretty much all the time, like even simple stuff—doing a load of laundry, going to open gym, or staying focused in class after a shift—takes way more effort than it used to, and no amount of sleeping in on my days off seems to really recharge me.

add_requirements.functional_impairment: Because I’m always dragging and down, I’ve started turning in assignments late, calling out or swapping shifts more often, and I barely see my friends or go to practices anymore, which is starting to worry my supervisor and my closest friend.
add_requirements.duration: Thinking back, this low, worn‑down way I’ve been feeling has been there pretty steadily since a few months after I started the rotating-shift inspector job while still doing classes, so a little over two years now.
